newsitem.title: UK: Canadian, British bonds fare best in week -Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Canadian, British bonds fare best in week -Salomon.

text.p: Canadian and British government bonds were top peformers in an extremely light but generally positive week, data from Salomon Brothers showed on Friday.

Canadian bonds returned 0.83 percent in local currency terms, grabbing the top spot among the 16 major sectors in the Salomon table. British bonds were not far behind, with a 0.79 percent return. Data were for the week ended Thursday.
For the dollar-based investor, those two markets were also the best performers, with British gilts giving a 1.39 percent return and Canadian debt 1.05 percent.
Japanese bonds were the week's lone losers.

Investors dumped Japanese government bonds (JGBs) amid speculation that a further fall in Japanese stocks will prompt profit-taking in order to cover for losses in equities. A raft of Japanese data had little net effect, analysts added.
JGBs lost 0.53 percent in yen and 1.30 percent in dollars.

Gilts rallied sharply just before Christmas holidays in what traders described as a short squeeze. Gilts, which had underperformed in recent weeks, are among the top yielders in Europe and have been touted by some analysts as a spread play.

There was little on the fundamental front to drive the market. Minutes of an October Bank of England/British Treasury monetary meeting were released on Monday but these were historical and the views that were revealed did not differ substantially from what the market had suspected, analysts said.

In Canada, markets posted several days of returns, and again fundamental factors were not cited as a major reason. The Bank of Canada on Monday conducted rounds of special purchase and resale agreemtns, stemming upward pressure on the overnight rate and adding liquidity to the system.
Data on Tuesday showed Canadian real gross domestic product in October rose 0.3 percent despite a 20-day auto sector strike.
European markets generally performed well. After gilts, Swedish bonds posted a 0.44 percent gain, Danish bonds a 0.41 percent return and Finnish bonds a 0.39 percent increase in local currency terms.

U.S. Treasuries were in positive territory but were among the laggards in the week, showing a 0.16 percent return. Benchmark Bunds were not much better, giving mark-based investors a 0.24 percent gain.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
